newsitem.title: USA: Apple debt unmoved despite two-notch ratings cut.
newsitem.headline: Apple debt unmoved despite two-notch ratings cut.

text.p: Bonds of Apple Computer Inc were unmoved despite a two-notch downgrade by a credit rating agency on the firm's long-term debt rating, traders said.
"There really hasn't been any movement in the paper ... I think the ratings cut was already priced in," said one high-yield trader.
Players said Apple debt was unchanged at 81-1/2 bid.
On Tuesday, Moody's cut the company's senior unsecured debt to B3 from B1 and the subordinated debt to Caa from B3.
Moody's said the downgrade to Apple's ratings was based on increasing business and financial risk to the company, stemming from its isolation in the Windows-dominated personal computer industry.
The rating agency also said Apple's historically strong debtholder protection measures will be under growing pressure near term.
